Marissa / Grace — quick heads up on Concordia. Elena from Concordia (cc'ed in our thread below) sent a procurement mandate that effectively conditions signature on two capabilities:

1) On-the-fly PII redaction applied at inference time (customer-side policy rules).
2) A non-reversible "redaction proof" artifact per request — a cryptographic hash-style snapshot that proves the original content was seen and redacted by our service without retaining raw PII.

Timing: procurement wants the feature demonstrated to legal by Oct 11 and DocuSign signature target is Oct 18. If we can commit to an opt-in pilot for Q4 they will move forward with the annual contract (>$1.2M ARR in first year).

Marissa — thanks for the context and the artifacts. A few clarifying questions from Product/Eng before we scope: 

1) Legal: does Concordia require the proof to be verifiable by a third party (e.g., auditor) or just internally by Concordia? That changes whether we need a public proof verification routine.
2) Redaction rules: are they fixed (regex lists) or do they want customer-supplied policies (complex: regex + ML PII classifier + per-route rules)?
3) Retention: what retention window for the proof artifacts? Is storing only hash+metadata for 90 days acceptable?
4) Performance: expected QPS at go-live? If they want low-latency (<200ms p99 for 256 tokens) that constrains approach.

Technical notes:
- We already have a content-filtering hook in the runtime but it currently replaces tokens and does not emit a cryptographic proof.
- Generating a non-reversible proof in-line is doable (hash redacted token positions + salt + HMAC), but we need a key management approach (KMS/HSM).
- Storing proofs securely and surfacing them via audit export will require changes to telemetry pipeline + storage tiering.

Can Ben/Grace forward any sample policy from Concordia and a rough QPS/latency expectation?

Irene
Irene Choi

On Wed, 29 Sep 2027 at 09:02, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com> wrote:
> Marissa — thanks for the context and the artifacts. A few clarifying questions from Product/Eng before we scope:

Thanks — adding initial scoping items and a proposed tradeoff path so we can make a call quickly: 

Proposed MVP (two-track):
A) Runtime hook: inference-time redact & emit "proof blob" = {route_id, request_id, salt, redacted_token_map, HMAC(signature)}. No raw content stored. Proofs encrypted at rest; keys via KMS.
B) Audit surface: export tool (UI + CSV) that returns per-request proof metadata and a verification utility for auditors (offline verifier).

Estimated effort (rough): 8–12 dev-weeks (core runtime + telemetry + QA + PM). Risks: KMS integration, p99 impact for small-payload flows, legal signoff on proof format.

Mitigation / canary: route-level opt-in behind Dedicated pools + feature flag + reduced retention window for pilot. If Concordia accepts an "opt-in pilot with dedicated capacity" we can limit exposure and accelerate rollout.

Next steps I propose:
- Immediate: Product will produce a 1-page scoping note and a minimal API contract (by Fri EOD). (I will own.)
- Engineering strawman: determine where proof blobs will live and rough cost estimate. (Need eng lead to confirm.)
- Customer: Ben/Grace to provide sample policies and QPS/latency targets.

Attaching scoping-notes.md (stub) for internal use.

Jordan Blake
